statement: The Commercial Act sets no minimum capital for a stock company. Article 329 governs share form only: par-value shares must carry a uniform par value of at least KRW 100 each, and the articles of incorporation may instead provide that all shares are no-par.
caveat: The former minimum-capital floor was removed in the small-company reform carried by the May 28, 2009 amendment (Act No. 9746, in force May 29, 2010) in the Act’s lineage; the old-version article text on law.go.kr renders only via script, so the repealed figure is not restated here. Sector licensing statutes (banking, insurance, capital markets and others) impose their own capital floors.
